policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere/ketiv is orthographic: ketiv באלפו is the defective spelling of the same 3ms suffix on a plural that the qere writes plene (בַּאֲלָפָ֔יו). ASV 'his thousands' is the reading both forms yield; nothing in the wording or notes distinguishes them, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.

Qere/ketiv is orthographic: ketiv ברבבתו is the defective spelling of the same 3ms suffix on a plural that the qere writes plene (בְּרִבְבֹתָֽיו). ASV 'his ten thousands' fits both forms equally; no wording or note distinguishes them, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.

Qere/ketiv is orthographic: ketiv ויתו and qere וַיְתָיו֙ are spellings of the same wayyiqtol of תוה. ASV 'scrabbled' (note 'Or, made marks' is alternative_rendering and concerns only the English gloss) renders the verb either way; nothing distinguishes the forms, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.
